findings.title: The publish rule is satisfied by any run text containing the command; a no-op or disabled publish step keeps the gate green
findings.where: scripts/verify-github-workflows.mjs, validateWorkflow() release.yml branch — publishSteps / publishRun (`step.run.includes("npm publish")` plus flag substring checks)
findings.why: The requirement says the gate must REQUIRE the publish step. It proves presence of text, not effective execution. Copy probes all exit 0 with no release-* issue: `run: npm publish --access public --provenance --dry-run` (npm's dry-run performs no upload), `if: false` on the step, `continue-on-error: true` (a failed publish would not fail the job), `run: echo "npm publish --access public --provenance"`, and `run: true || npm publish --access public --provenance`. Each is a one-line drift that silently stops publishing while the gate — and every CI run — stays green. This is the exact failure mode the new rule exists to prevent.
findings.direction: Assert the effective step, not a substring: require the publish step's run to trim-equal `npm publish --access public --provenance`, reject `--dry-run`, and reject a step carrying `if`, `continue-on-error`, `env` or `with`. Optionally also assert the step is the only publish step and that no earlier step shares its name.

findings.title: Tokenless rule is a four-literal denylist; a legacy token-auth publish step passes
findings.where: scripts/verify-github-workflows.mjs, validateWorkflow() — the loop over ["NPM_TOKEN", "NODE_AUTH_TOKEN", "_authToken", ".npmrc"] on JSON.stringify(data)
findings.why: A copy whose publish step sets `env: LEGACY_PUBLISH_SECRET: ${{ secrets.LEGACY_PUBLISH_SECRET }}` and runs `npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:username npm` + `npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_password "$(...|base64)"` + `npm publish --access public --provenance` exits 0 with no release-* issue. The named literals (verified by the shipped control) are caught, but the property the requirement states — FORBID token-based npm auth — is not: `_auth`/`_password` and an arbitrary secret name are outside the blocklist. A blocklist cannot prove the absence of token auth.
findings.direction: Make the publish step's shape positive: no `env`, no `with`, exact run (which also closes the High finding). If a blocklist stays, add `_password`, `_auth`, `username`/`npm config set` and any `secrets.` reference inside the publish step, and ship a control for the legacy form.

findings.title: No shipped self-test control for release-npm-publish-order, although the requirement asks for a control per rule
findings.where: scripts/verify-github-workflows.mjs, runSelfTest() fixtures list (28 fixtures + 1 missing-workflow = 29)
findings.why: The rule fires correctly (a copy with the publish block moved after softprops/action-gh-release exits 1 with release-npm-publish-order), but nothing in the shipped self-test exercises it: at HEAD there were 25 fixtures + 1; the change adds exactly three (release-npm-publish, release-id-token, release-npm-tokenless). The requirement says the script must 'ship falsifiable negative controls for each'. Deleting the order rule from the validator would leave --self-test at 29/29 green.
findings.direction: Add one fixture that moves NPM_PUBLISH_STEP after the GitHub Release step and expects release-npm-publish-order (29 -> 30 fixtures, 30/30), and optionally a second that moves it before npm pack.

findings.title: CHANGELOG Unreleased describes what it supersedes as 'unmeasured', while the 0.7.0 note actually asserts 'not published (npm view returns 404)'
findings.where: CHANGELOG.md, Unreleased > Changed, first bullet vs the 0.7.0 > Added install bullet
findings.why: The new bullet says it supersedes 'the 0.7.0 note that the registry form was unmeasured'; the superseded sentence makes the stronger, now-false claim that 0.7.0 is not published. A reader landing on the 0.7.0 section still reads a present-tense falsehood. Changelog history should not be rewritten, so this is wording, not a defect.
findings.direction: Reword the supersession to name the actual claim ('the 0.7.0 note that the package was not published'), or add a one-line pointer at the 0.7.0 entry.

findings.title: CONTRIBUTING (both languages) says the release assert accepts `vX.Y.Z` and `X.Y.Z`, but the workflow only triggers on `tags: ['v*']`
findings.where: CONTRIBUTING.md and CONTRIBUTING.zh-CN.md, release workflow table row (modified by this change)
findings.why: The modified row re-asserts an internally contradictory claim: an `X.Y.Z` tag never starts release.yml, so the assert's `#v` tolerance is unreachable for that form. Pre-existing text, but re-touched here.
findings.direction: Drop 'and `X.Y.Z`' from the row, or widen the trigger to `tags: ['v*', '[0-9]*']` if the form is intended.

declinedToJudge: Trusted Publisher configuration on npmjs — cannot be read anonymously (404 endpoints, unsigned 0.7.0); recorded INCONCLUSIVE, not a finding.
0.7.0 has no provenance attestation and was published by a user account — docs explicitly say it predates the OIDC step; the requirement demands provenance only for future tag publishes.
Publish-before-GHCR/GitHub-Release means a later image/release failure leaves an immutable npm version published — the frozen requirement mandates this exact order.
Historical CHANGELOG 0.7.0 'not published (404)' sentence — changelog history is a record of that release; the Unreleased bullet supersedes it. Only the wording nit above is raised.
npm publish re-runs the manifest's `prepack` guard (verify-package-files.mjs) against dist/silicon-package — pre-existing lifecycle behaviour, not introduced here; it passed after the pack step.
Comment lines in release.yml naming NPM_TOKEN/.npmrc — comments are not a token step; the requirement bans token steps and the gate intentionally scans semantic values only.
Registry *install* path (`dsh plugin add ... @mpd-dsh/silicon@0.7.0`) not re-measured — docs state this bound explicitly; running it needs a real dsh profile and a writable HOME.
docker-verify.yml / boot-e2e.yml unchanged and not re-run — outside this change set.
The npm publish tarball is the root package while the prepack guard checks the rewritten staged package — pre-existing design; not part of the requirement and no failure observed.

A second publish step after the GitHub Release is not detected when an earlier valid publish step exists (publishSteps[0] only) — contrived; covered by the High finding's 'assert the publish step' direction.
bounds: The real GitHub Actions tag run is UNPROVEN: no OIDC token exchange, no npm provenance attestation, no actual v0.7.1 publish was performed (no tag, no credentials). Only the workflow definition and the offline gate were measured.
The npmjs Trusted Publisher binding (repo + workflow filename) is UNPROVEN: not exposed anonymously.
Did not run docker-verify.yml or boot-e2e.yml (Docker image build, real harness boots); out of scope for this change set.
Did not run the registry install path end to end (needs a writable HOME/dsh profile).
Did not re-derive the published 0.7.0 tarball from this working tree; only its registry metadata, downloaded sha1 and file count were measured.

Read: the full 10-file diff, release.yml, the gate script's validation/self-test regions, the doc diffs, package.json, AGENTS.md/AGENT.md. Not read line-by-line: the untouched parts of scripts/verify-github-workflows.mjs (lines 1-380, 580-680) beyond what the diff and runs exercise.
verdictJustification: The workflow and docs are correct and every mandated check passes, but the new gate rules can be satisfied by a no-op/disabled publish step and by a legacy token-auth step, and the publish-order rule ships no self-test control — so the requirement's 'REQUIRE the publish step' and 'negative controls for each' clauses are not fully met.
